title: Impact of Sleep, Fatigue and Systemic Inflammation on Neurocognitive and Behavioral Outcomes in Long-term Survivors of Childhood Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
notes: Cross-sectional study of 70 childhood ALL survivors (50% male, mean age 14.3yr, 7.4yr post-diagnosis) treated on Total Therapy XV at St Jude. Chemo-only (no cranial radiation). Concurrent neurocognitive testing, behavioral ratings, sleep quality, fatigue, and serum biomarkers (IL-1beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha, hsCRP, MDA, MPO, OxLDL). ALL analyses stratified by sex. KEY FINDING: Strong sex-specific effects — females showed fatigue-cognition and inflammation-cognition associations but males did not (except TNF-alpha → organization). Survivors performed below population norms on executive function and processing speed. Inflammatory biomarker-cognition associations (IL-6, IL-1beta, hsCRP → worse exec function/processing speed in females) shown in figures as tertile comparisons only — no continuous effect sizes extractable for OIC edges. NOTE: pediatric sample may not generalize directly to adult CRCI.
effect_size_notes: Fatigue-cognition correlations (r) converted to d via 2r/sqrt(1-r^2). N for females estimated at ~35 (half of 70, stratified by sex). Paper uses Z-score adjusted cognitive measures and GLM adjusted for age. The r=0.56 for fatigue-processing speed is from the abstract; the 0.36-0.55 range for attention covers multiple attention subtests. These are within-group associations (no control group).

inflammatory_findings.IL6_exec_function_females: Higher IL-6 tertile → worse cognitive flexibility and processing speed in females (Figure 3, P's<.05)
inflammatory_findings.IL1beta_exec_processing_females: Higher IL-1beta → worse organization and visual-motor processing speed in females (Figure 3, P's<.05)
inflammatory_findings.hsCRP_multiple_females: Higher hsCRP → worse executive function, processing speed, attention in females (Figure 3, P's<.05)
inflammatory_findings.TNFa_organization_males: Higher TNF-alpha → worse organization in males (P=.03)
inflammatory_findings.IL1beta_fatigue: Higher IL-1beta → greater cognitive fatigue in females (P=.002)
inflammatory_findings.IL1beta_sleep: Higher IL-1beta → longer sleep duration in females (P<.001)
inflammatory_findings.note: All biomarker analyses use tertile comparisons, not continuous regression — cannot extract continuous effect sizes

sex_specific_note: Effects are almost exclusively in females. Extraction uses female-only n≈35, not full sample of 70.
